correctness.rationale: Reconstructed the conductance-normalized transition matrix, the antisymmetric \(-t/(b+t)\) eigenmode and all zero modes, the 3-class quotient for \(a\ge3\) and a separate 2-class quotient for \(a=2\). Vieta formulas give exact \(K(t)\) for all \(a\ge2,b\ge1,t\ge0\). Differentiation yields a one-positive-root stationary polynomial and a unique global minimum; monotonicity in \(a\) proves the sharp \(-1/6\) lower bound with equality exactly \(a=2,t=b\). Balanced asymptotics follow by bounding the positive root and passing to a rational-function limit. 790 exact rational computational assertions include 240 direct full-matrix Kemeny comparisons and checks at boundaries, all executed successfully. Finite tests support rather than prove universal quantifiers.

originality.rationale: 2019 Hu–Kirkland Theorem 2.0.1 explicitly proves the \(t=1\) specialization, so that specialization is credited and excluded. Its spectral treatment does not classify varying positive conductance; 2022 Altafini et al. provide generic weighted-edge perturbation algebra but not the unique biclique optimizer, sign-transition curve or sharp uniform \(-1/6\) bound. 2021 Faught–Kempton–Knudson applies to 1-separable graphs; 2023 Kirkland–Li–McAlister–Zhang studies unit-edge insertions into trees. The claim is the global continuous-conductance classification and extremal bound, not novelty of the spectrum formula machinery. Actual indexed scholarly and literature searches found no explicit equivalent; generic weighted methods could imply it after further specialization, and incomplete historical coverage remains a residual risk.
residual_risks: General weighted inverse-matrix formulas can in principle be specialized to the biclique family; claim is a newly worked-out sharp design classification rather than an independent generic mechanism.
Search coverage cannot establish historical priority; an unindexed or inaccessible weighted biclique-specific treatment could be equivalent.
Full-text examination of all possible later papers was not feasible; abstract-only papers are not asserted to rule out all coverage.

value.rationale: A natural network-design question (how strongly to add a link) has a counterintuitive answer: every weak new link improves Kemeny while an ordinary unit link can worsen it; the exact family-wide optimal conductance is unique and the maximum possible gain is sharply \(-1/6\) with an attained equality family. The balanced \(n\ge9\) sign reversal separates conductance optimization from the known edge insertion problem. This is a complete structural classification of a motivated parameter, not a mere renamed instance, a numerical table, or an unmotivated small-case increment.
